No revival, so the top rescue rung is earned on prevention plus restoration plus no-action outward temp HP rather than on a heal ceiling.

paladin/Oath of Devotion.why: The bare paladin chassis with a charm-immunity aura bolted on: Improved Divine Smite is the scaling rider that holds st at rung 3, Revivify plus Lay on Hands is the rescue floor, and nothing here adds a third attack source or any area answer.
uncertain: Aura of Devotion's charm immunity is prevention aimed at the partner, but narrow enough that it does not clear the rung-4 clause; rsc stays 3.

Aura of Protection (+Cha to the partner's saves) is the largest pair-level Saves effect in the game and is invisible here — sav is null by contract and the rubric says auras are a pair flag, not this body's score. True of every entry in this batch.
Purity of Spirit (15) and Holy Nimbus (20) are outside Act II and are not counted.

paladin/Oath of the Ancients.why: Aura of Warding is proportional resistance to spell damage covering both bodies at 9m, which is simultaneously this body's mitigation layer above heavy-and-shield and unconditional prevention aimed at the partner — the damage type this modlist's rebuilt casters lean on hardest.
uncertain: Ice Storm and Stoneskin arrive with the 13 oath spells and 4th-tier slots at Paladin 13, right at the edge of the 12-13 judging point; aoe 2 assumes they are just online.
Aura of Protection is a pair-level Saves effect not carried by this schema.
Listo's global aura patch nominally normalises paladin auras to 9m/15m; scores assume it applies.

paladin/Oath of Vengeance.why: Haste on the partner at Paladin 9 is the Actions ladder's rung-5 clause bought on a half-caster, and Vow of Enmity is blanket Advantage on a short-rest charge — scale-invariant, and worth more with Lone Wolf's doubled attack count than in a normal party.
uncertain: act 4 rather than 5 because Haste costs the one concentration slot and there is no Action Surge or summon set under it; the same slot is what stops ctrl_s rising, since Hold Person and Banishment want it too.
Vow of Enmity is accuracy rather than damage; st 4 reads it as the 'repeatable burst channel' clause on a short-rest clock and could defensibly be 3.
Aura of Protection is a pair-level Saves effect not carried by this schema.

paladin/Oath of the Crown.why: Spirit Guardians on a heavy-armour body is the rubric's own Act II anchor for repeatable AoE and moving area denial at once, and Champion Challenge is a no-concentration area taunt on a short-rest charge that pulls fire off the squishier half.
uncertain: Crown's vanilla oath spell list was not in the read set; Spirit Guardians and Aura of Vitality at oath level 9 are taken from standard BG3 Crown and drive aoe 3, ctrl_a 3 and the concentration flag. If they are not on the list here, aoe drops to 1 and ctrl_a to 2.
Divine Allegiance is damage redirection, which the rubric caps at rung 1 in a duo and which actively hurts this body; it is not scored above the baseline anywhere.
Royal Decree cantrip from mod.io is recorded as unverified in the class file and is not scored.
Aura of Protection is a pair-level Saves effect not carried by this schema.

paladin/Oathbreaker.why: Spiteful Suffering is a per-turn damage channel that also hands out Advantage, stacked under Improved Unholy Smite and Aura of Hate, and Animate Dead at 9 plus Control Undead is real body count; Dreadful Aspect is area Frighten off a short-rest charge with no concentration.
uncertain: Every smite is Necrotic and never Radiant — a straight downgrade against exactly the shadow-cursed and undead population of Act II. st 4 rests on the physical attack routine and Aura of Hate, not on the smite payload, and 3 is defensible.
Aura of Hate buffs 'you and nearby fiends and undead', so a normal partner gets nothing; it is scored as this body's damage only.
StackId means Animate Dead replaces rather than accumulates, so act 3 counts one maintained body, not several.
Aura of Protection is a pair-level Saves effect not carried by this schema.

paladin/Oath of Conquest.why: Conquering Presence is area hard control on a short-rest charge that spends no concentration — the rung-4 clause outright — and Aura of Conquest then taxes everything it lands on; Spiritual Weapon adds the bonus-action attack the class otherwise lacks and Guided Strike guarantees the one roll that must land.
uncertain: The aura's speed-reduction-to-0 clause does nothing in BG3 per the mod author, so Aura of Conquest is only the psychic tick; aoe 2 prices it as far under Act II par in magnitude while repeatable in shape.
ctrl_a 4 rests on BG3's Frightened being worth a rung, which is weaker than the tabletop condition; if Frightened is read as a soft debuff this is 3.
Invincible Conqueror, the capstone the class file rates highest for a duo, is level 20 and outside Act II.
Aura of Protection is a pair-level Saves effect not carried by this schema.

paladin/Oath of the Bleak Walkers.why: Black Flames is a repeatable burst channel on a short-rest charge that also Sickens the target's Constitution saves, Death's Maw is a proficiency-bonus flat reduction that lasts until long rest, and Expertise in Intimidation at level 1 is the only Skills rung anywhere in this batch — it clears Act I's Hag's Hair gate outright on a stat the oath already maxes.
uncertain: Death's Maw's damage reduction requires standing within 2m of a corpse; dur 4 assumes that is trivially satisfied after the first kill, which is true in most but not all fights, and the reduction is flat and therefore boss-weighted-act unfriendly.
The level 7 crit-range aura buffs the partner's offence, which lands on no axis this schema carries for this body.
Feature names come from the mod's prose and changelog rather than the pak; the oathbreaking behaviour is recorded as unverified.
Aura of Protection is a pair-level Saves effect not carried by this schema.

paladin/Oath of the Moon (Selûne-inspire.why: The only oath carrying prevention in two forms at once — Aura of Moonlight's flat -Cha on every hit either body takes, and Divine Guardian halving all damage on the partner for ten turns off a short-rest charge — with Full Moon as slot-free area Blind-and-Slow under it and Spirit Guardians at 9.
uncertain: dur 4 rather than 5: the oath supplies both a flat reduction and a halving without spending a feat, but the rubric reserves Act II rung 5 for a Shield Master plus Tough stack, which this profile does not assume.
Lunar Champion's party-wide save bonus and extra Reaction are level 20 and outside Act II.
Aura radius under Listo's global aura patch is recorded as unverified for a v10.0-era subclass.
Aura of Protection is a pair-level Saves effect not carried by this schema.

paladin/Oath of Illumination.why: Scored as the bare paladin chassis, because that is all that is verifiable: the oath layer has no published level-by-level feature list anywhere, and Listo added the pack 'for testing'.
uncertain: Every value above is the class chassis, not the oath. The only feature name recoverable is Aura of Brilliance and its mechanics are unknown. Do not read any of these ten as a claim about the oath.

The pitch is a ranged radiant paladin. If that holds, aoe and st are both understated and the body takes no reach discount on single-target damage — a materially different shape from every other entry. Worth a human confirming in game before the ledger uses this row.
Aura of Protection is a pair-level Saves effect not carried by this schema.

paladin/Supporting library.why: This heading is the Oath Framework (6493) note — an API for custom paladin mods to declare oathbreaking and redemption triggers, not player-facing content and not selectable. The class file records that nothing in the 10.2 paladin set is confirmed to use it: Bleak Walkers removed its Oath Framework files, Conquest piggybacks on Vengeance's oathbreaking and Moon on Devotion's.

paragon/Lionheart.why: Banners count as attacks for Extra Attack, so post-5 you banner AND swing: Red hands the partner a reaction attack with a Willpower Die on it, Yellow moves +CHA AC onto the squishier half, and level 6 puts the whole pool on the short-rest clock. Vanguard's Charge at 9 is blanket Disadvantage on attacks against you.
uncertain: dur 4 reads Vanguard's Charge's blanket Disadvantage as the ladder's 'damage-halving source' on top of heavy armour and shield; it only applies after your first turn in combat, so the opening round is rung 3.
act 4 not 5: Red Banner hands the partner a Reaction attack, not an Action, and Banner Charges are only CHA-modifier many per short rest from level 6.
Legendary Banner's free-attack-every-turn is level 17 and does not touch Act II.

paragon/Nighthawk.why: Searing Blade strips ALL resistances for 3 turns on a failed Con save — the rubric names Paragon Nighthawk as one of the list's resistance strips — and Supernatural Dampening then blocks the target's healing and treats it as sunlit, while Iron Filings stacks 1d4 Fire per turn and Scorching Rebuke burns whoever hits you.
uncertain: Nighthawk's own damage is locked to Fire, which Absolute Wrath caps at 4 from Act II; the subclass escapes the cap only by stripping the resistance first, so st 4 is contingent on Searing Blade's Con save landing.
ctrl_s 3 rests on Bird Cage, which arrives at 13 — the exact judging level — and is a leash (stay within 6m or take 1d10) rather than a lockdown.
rsc 3: Vigilant Aegis puts Protection from Evil and Good on the partner through Help, which is prevention, but there is no healing or revival anywhere in the class.

paragon/Prodigy.why: Sheer Will's temp HP carries a flat -2 damage from every source at Paragon 9, which lands AFTER Lone Wolf's halving and is therefore worth double, and Training From Hell adds non-magical physical resistance at 13; Competitive Streak refunds Willpower Dice off the partner's natural 20s, so the pool is fed by someone else's rolls.
uncertain: dur 4 not 5: the Act II rung-5 row wants roughly flat -6 after halving plus Evasion-grade AoE mitigation, and Prodigy reaches -2 plus one proportional layer. The flat half is crowd-facing and worth less in a boss-weighted act, per the rubric's own note.
Innate Mastery's +1/+2 to attack and damage is flat and slips against the HP curve, so st stays at 3.
Echo of the Soul's ally-count scaling is nearly dead in a duo (+1d10, not +5d10) and is level 17 regardless.

paragon/Regent.why: Shifting Court swaps your position with the partner's on a Willpower Die, which is the direct answer to a duo's worst failure mode, and Fairy's Curse strips a crit target's Bonus Actions and Reactions and halves its movement — action-economy denial that costs no concentration.
uncertain: rsc 3: the position swap is close to the damage-redirection pattern the brief caps at rung 1 — it moves the danger from one half of the pair to the other. It scored above 1 only because the armoured body genuinely eats it better and it is repositioning rather than damage transfer. A human may want to force this to 1.
ctrl_s 3 not 4: Fairy's Curse is crit-gated, and although Strike Of The Butterflies drops the crit threshold by 2 at level 9 it is still not a per-turn effect.
Oberon's Favor consumes one stack per weapon attack against a CHA-mod stack pool, so it does not ride every swing of a four-attack Lone Wolf round without spending dice.

paragon/Spellblade — the exception the s.why: Scholar's Armament makes the main-hand melee weapon use Charisma for attack and damage, which is the only genuinely single-stat body in the class, and Spell Sword attacks count as cantrips that work with Extra Attack — six Focuses by 17 means six damage types against Absolute Wrath's layered resistances, with Arcane Surge scaling them off Willpower Dice.
uncertain: ctrl_s 3 rests on Will Over Weave, a slot-free Counterspell on a short-rest die, which arrives at exactly 13 — the judging level. At 12 this reads 1.
aoe 2: the Force and Thunder Focuses (Slashing Blades, Shattering Slam) hit enemies around the target at will, which is repeatable, but at 1d6+CHA it is far under the Act II rung-3 anchor.

Potent Robe adds Charisma to cantrip damage and Spell Sword attacks are 'considered cantrips' — the equipment file flags whether the robe actually fires on them as unverified. If it does, st is understated.

paragon/Sword Saint.why: Falling Rain is a FREE-ACTION melee attack riding every Willpower Die you already spend, so Lone Wolf's second Action doubles the Blade Skills and therefore doubles the free attacks; Disciple of Steel and Strategy refunds dice off your own natural 20s, which makes the loop close on itself.
uncertain: Falling Rain uses 1d4 in place of the weapon's damage dice, so each free attack is small — st 4 is scored on attack count and rider stacking, not on the size of the extra swings.
act 4 not 5: free-action attacks are an unbounded extra attack source but not an Action handed to the other body, which is the rung-5 clause.
Wisdom of Void wants 6 Willpower Dice, exactly the level-17 pool, so the auto-crit round is Act III and pairs with Beyond All Limits at 18.

ranger/Beast Master (base game + `Expans.why: Expansion moves Companion's Bond to level 3 and adds a Panther that uses your proficiency bonus, is proficient in all saving throws, takes your ASIs and can Help as a bonus action — a permanent third body on a short-rest re-summon, on top of the Conjure Animals set every Ranger gets at 9.
uncertain: act 4 assumes Conjure Animals is the non-concentration-until-long-rest version the rubric attributes to mod 13458; if that mod does not reach the Ranger list it is concentration and act falls to 3.
The companion's Help action can stand a downed partner back up, which is arguably Rescue; it was left out of rsc because it spends the companion's action, not this body's.

ranger/Gloom Stalker (base game + `Expan.why: Stalker's Flurry at 11 re-attacks free on every miss, which is a third attack source on top of Extra Attack and Hunter's Mark, and Shadowy Dodge plus Umbral Shroud convert Lone Wolf's spare reaction into mitigation the medium-armour chassis otherwise lacks.
uncertain: MATERIAL: Iron Mind at level 7 grants Wisdom AND Intelligence saving throw proficiency, which patches the Ranger's worst structural weakness — but `prof` records only the level-1 class grant, so this profile's derived sav understates Gloom Stalker by two disjoint saves including Wisdom. A human should decide whether the schema needs to carry subclass-granted saves.
Dread Ambusher's extra attack and +3 initiative are first-turn only and were not scored in act.

ranger/Hunter (base game + `Expansion`).why: Volley at 11 is the rubric's own Act II rung-5 AoE anchor — full weapon damage to every target, no save, no resource — and Lone Wolf's second Action fires it twice a round; Defensive Tactics and Superior Hunter's Defense add mitigation on top.
uncertain: Colossus Slayer's +1d8 is a flat rider and slips against Combat Extender's HP curve, which is why st stays at 3.
Superior Hunter's Defense (Evasion or Uncanny Dodge) lands at 15, the very top of the Act II band, so dur 3 is scored on Multiattack Defence rather than on it.

ranger/Swarmkeeper (base game, Patch 8 +.why: Gathered Swarm fires once per round after any attack with no resource and no concentration, and the Flurry of Moths option applies Blind — a repeatable free single-target lockdown — while the teleport option is the answer to being focused when there is no third body to peel.
uncertain: ctrl_s 3 rests on the Moths Blind rider; a Swarmkeeper who picks Jellyfish or Bees for the damage instead reads ctrl_s 1.
The swarm is 1d6 rising to 1d8 at 11 — flat and small, so it adds nothing above the rung-3 st reading.
Web off long-rest slots is explicitly background by Act II, hence ctrl_a 2.

ranger/Drakewarden.why: The drake is a permanent third body whose Infused Strikes adds 1d6 of its essence type when ANY creature within 30ft hits with a weapon attack — so it buffs the partner too — and Reflexive Resistance is a second life-saving reaction Lone Wolf makes affordable.
uncertain: end 3 rather than 4: Drake's Breath, the free re-summon and Reflexive Resistance are all long-rest pools, which is heavier long-rest dependence than the other conclaves carry.
Reflexive Resistance reaches the drake or the Ranger, NOT the partner, so it scored in dur and not in rsc.
The mod author warns a new playthrough may be needed for the drake to animate correctly.

ranger/Fey Wanderer.why: Otherworldly Glamour adds the Wisdom modifier to every Charisma check plus a Charisma skill proficiency, which makes the Ranger the party face with no Charisma investment at all; Counterspell arrives at class 9 and Fey Reinforcements is a free Summon Fey from 11.
uncertain: skl 3 is scored on breadth plus a doubled modifier rather than true Expertise, and the rubric's Act II rung-2 row says a broad list with no Expertise is rung 1 — the doubled Wisdom modifier is what carries it, by analogy to Vengeance's Monster Tactician.
Fey Reinforcements' non-concentration variant is behind a toggle with a 1-minute duration; act 4 assumes the toggle is on.
Misty Wanderer (15) only resolves reliably in turn-based mode per the class file.

ranger/Horizon Walker.why: Planar Warrior converts ALL of an attack's damage to Force and adds 2d8 from 11, which deletes Absolute Wrath's layered resistances outright, and it costs a bonus action rather than concentration — so Haste at class 9 is free to sit in the concentration slot; Distant Strike is a genuine third attack whenever three enemies are present.
uncertain: act 4 credits Haste on the partner; the ladder's rung 5 additionally wants this body's own extra attacks plus a summon set, which Horizon Walker does not have.
Distant Strike's third attack requires attacking two different creatures first, so it is not available in a single-target boss round.
Ethereal Step is wasted outside turn-based mode per the class file.

ranger/Monster Slayer.why: The only conclave whose damage rider costs no concentration, so Slayer's Prey stacks with Hunter's Mark, and Magic-User's Nemesis is a slot-free counterspell-equivalent on a short-rest clock — with Hunter's Sense turning one hit per use into a full resistance and immunity bypass.
uncertain: Supernatural Defense (+1d6 on every save the prey forces) and Slayer's Counter (auto-succeed a save on a hit) are large save effects that the schema cannot express, because sav is derived from the level-1 prof pair alone. This understates Monster Slayer's boss-fight resilience.
Hold Monster is subclass spell level 17 and Banishment 13, so ctrl_s 3 rests on Magic-User's Nemesis in Act II.

ranger/Primeval Guardian (UA).why: The only Ranger that is a tank: guardian form gives temp HP equal to half Ranger level every turn and +2 max HP per Ranger level from 7, all at no action and no resource — bought with a movement speed of 5 ft, which is a steep price this profile does not otherwise register.
uncertain: Guardian Aura at 15 heals a hurt partner half your Ranger level every turn with no action — a rung-4 Rescue effect landing at the very top of the Act II band. Judged at 12-13 it is not yet online, so rsc reads 3; at 15 it is 4.
Rooted Defense is difficult terrain, which the ladder pins at rung 1, so it did not lift ctrl_a above the Entangle/Grasping Vine reading.
dur 3 not 4: the temp HP and max HP layers are effective HP, not the flat-reduction or halving source the rung-4 clause names.

ranger/Snowlight Conclave.why: Glaring Frost forces a Con save vs your spell DC for Blind on EVERY instance of Cold or Radiant damage, at no resource and no concentration, so a Ranger making four-plus attacks a round under Lone Wolf blinds a room; Snow Blindness then taxes every action those blinded enemies take.
uncertain: MATERIAL: both control scores are entirely gear-conditional — the conclave needs a Cold or Radiant damage source to function at all, and the class file says so outright. With no such weapon this reads ctrl_s 1 / ctrl_a 1. This is the widest swing in my set.
ctrl_a 4 is the no-concentration clause applied to a multi-attack blind routine; the true area version, Snowborn Anthelion, is level 15.
Snow Blindness's 1d6 radiant per enemy action is flat and small, so aoe stays at 2.

ranger/Conclave of the Dawnstriders.why: The highest raw damage ceiling of the eleven: Extra Attack plus Valkyrie's landing attack, Zeal's extra attack every seven swings, and Divine Flurry's five extra attacks at a reduced crit threshold off a 3rd-level slot — with Herald of the Sun converting weapon damage to Radiant or Fire to dodge physical resistance.
uncertain: st 4 not 5 because Act II's rung 5 is anchored on Improved Extra Attack (Fighter 11); Divine Flurry was read as the 'repeatable burst channel' clause of rung 4 instead.
Divine Flurry leaves you Faded (-2 attack rolls per stack) until the end of your next turn, which in a party with no third body is a real cost — it is a fight-ending button, not a rotation.
The mod author swapped Zeal and Valkyrie in 1.2.0.66, so the level-3 pick in 10.2 is Valkyrie.

rogue/Thief.why: Fast Hands is a second Bonus Action, so with Lone Wolf this body has three - three off-hand strikes a round on top of the two Action attacks, which is the third attack source the Rogue chassis otherwise lacks. Supreme Sneak is short-rest invisibility and Use Magic Device at 13 ignores every item requirement in a list stuffed with branded gear. Sneak Attack is at-will with no clock, which is the top of Endurance by definition.
uncertain: Thief's Reflexes (17) is Act III and the author warns it breaks in inescapable combats and misbehaves with shared ally turns - exactly the situation a two-player party is in.
Fast Hands does not stack with the Thief's Apprentice feat.

Single-target control is Cunning Strike only - a repeatable non-concentration Prone/Poison/Disarm rider with no control spell under it. Scored at the rung-2 band because Prone is not turn-removal against Act II bodies.

rogue/Assassin.why: Alacrity restores an Action and a Bonus Action at combat start and Assassinate grants advantage against anything that has not acted, which Listo's d10+Dex initiative makes reliable. But all of it is round one: against Combat Extender's +126% regular and +170% boss HP, fights last long enough that an opener is a smaller share of the total than it reads, and Assassin contributes least in the long reinforced fights where the duo is most at risk.
uncertain: Death Strike and Imposter are 17 and 13; the 13 piece is in band but is an out-of-combat setup tool rather than a combat rung.

Single-target control is Cunning Strike only - a repeatable non-concentration Prone/Poison/Disarm rider with no control spell under it. Scored at the rung-2 band because Prone is not turn-removal against Act II bodies.

rogue/Arcane Trickster.why: The only Rogue with a control list. Magical Ambush at 9 gives every one of its spells disadvantage on the target's saves while Hiding, and Cunning Action Hide makes that a bonus-action at-will condition rather than a setup - disadvantage-on-saves is the form that does not decay. Shadow Blade, Hold Person, Hypnotic Pattern, Fear and Enemies Abound are all in reach by spell level 3. The cost is Int competing with Dex on a third-caster slot table.
uncertain: Third-caster progression puts spell level 3 at class 13, so at the low end of the judging band the control list is still 2nd tier.
Spell Thief (17) is script-extender implemented and may fail to register on AoE, cone and line spells.

rogue/Swashbuckler.why: The only Rogue that gets Sneak Attack without a setup body, which is the exact hole a two-character party has - there is often no second melee to flank with. Dirty Tricks are at-will Disarm, Blind and attack-disadvantage riders costing no concentration, and Panache is a repeatable contested charm that catches bystanders. Cha-based tricks also make it the natural party face.
uncertain: SEVERE for a mono-20 read: Swashbuckler has no subclass features at all from 13 to 20, and the RAW Rakish Sneak Attack rework in Goon's 2.x is absent from the 1.2.2.0 build Listo ships. The Act II value here is close to its permanent ceiling.
Dirty Tricks DCs key off Charisma, which is not this body's primary.

rogue/Inquisitive.why: The out-of-combat ceiling of the class. Steady Eye is flat advantage on Perception and Investigation with the 5e half-movement restriction dropped, Ear for Deceit puts a floor of 8 on the Insight die, and Reliable Talent plus four Expertise picks means passive Perception sits in the 20s and Sleight of Hand clears Araj - both named Act II gates on one body, which is what rung 5 is. Insightful Fighting is also a repeatable no-ally Sneak Attack enabler.
uncertain: No Guidance (no spell list), which the Skills rungs from 3 up assume; scored on gates cleared rather than on the literal rung text.
Unerring Eye's uses scale on Wisdom, which a Dex/Con Rogue will not have.

Single-target control is Cunning Strike only - a repeatable non-concentration Prone/Poison/Disarm rider with no control spell under it. Scored at the rung-2 band because Prone is not turn-removal against Act II bodies.

rogue/Mastermind.why: Master of Tactics turns Help into a Bonus Action, and in a duo Help is how you pick the other half of your action economy up off the floor - doing it without spending an Action, at will, on a body that has two Bonus Actions, is a better clock than Revivify has. It also hands the partner advantage as a bonus action, which feeds smites and big single hits. Misdirection is redirection and is priced as such.
uncertain: Insightful Manipulator's save penalty scales on Wisdom, a poor fit for a Dex build.
Misdirection needs a body within 2 m, which in a duo means aiming the hit at your only partner - net zero at best.

Single-target control is Cunning Strike only - a repeatable non-concentration Prone/Poison/Disarm rider with no control spell under it. Scored at the rung-2 band because Prone is not turn-removal against Act II bodies.

rogue/Phantom.why: Whispers of the Dead grants proficiency in every skill of a chosen ability once per short rest, on demand, which combined with four Expertise picks and Reliable Talent clears the Act II gates whichever ability they turn out to sit behind. Wails from the Grave is the only Rogue answer to two targets at once. Ghost Walk at 13 is disadvantage on every attack against you for the fight, on top of Evasion and Uncanny Dodge, and Soul Trinkets fund it from kills rather than rests - which is the currency Listo actually charges for.
uncertain: Wails from the Grave is PB uses per long rest plus trinkets; it is a second-target rider, not area damage, so it stays at the incidental rung.
The Cunning Strike compatibility patch was authored against Book of Rogues 1.0.0.2 while Listo ships 1.0.0.3, and its author states he did not test the level 17 features.

Single-target control is Cunning Strike only - a repeatable non-concentration Prone/Poison/Disarm rider with no control spell under it. Scored at the rung-2 band because Prone is not turn-removal against Act II bodies.

rogue/Scout.why: Survivalist is two free Expertise picks, taking the body to six, and Ambush Master at 13 is +5 initiative plus a first-round mark that gives everyone advantage on that target - a party-wide buff is worth double when the party is two. Skirmisher gives the spare reaction a use. Otherwise this is the base Rogue chassis; its own combat surplus arrives at 17 with Sudden Strike.
uncertain: Alert is only +Proficiency Bonus in this list, which is what makes a flat +5 competitive; that comparison is act-dependent.

Single-target control is Cunning Strike only - a repeatable non-concentration Prone/Poison/Disarm rider with no control spell under it. Scored at the rung-2 band because Prone is not turn-removal against Act II bodies.

rogue/Soulknife.why: The most self-sufficient Rogue: weapon, accuracy fix, mobility and invisibility all come out of one pool, so it needs no gear and no ally. Homing Strikes is miss-insurance that only spends the die on a hit, which matters disproportionately when one body's turn is a quarter of the round. Psi-Bolstered Knack lifts skill checks off the same pool.
uncertain: SEVERE: the number and size of Psionic Energy Dice and their recovery rate are not stated anywhere the class file could read - Restore Psionic Energy exists as an activated ability but its clock is unknown. Every Soulknife feature is priced in that currency, so `end` and `dur` here are the Rogue chassis, not a reading of the subclass economy.
Psychic is one of the more commonly resisted damage types late, and Psychic Blades deal psychic rather than weapon damage.

Single-target control is Cunning Strike only - a repeatable non-concentration Prone/Poison/Disarm rider with no control spell under it. Scored at the rung-2 band because Prone is not turn-removal against Act II bodies.

rogue/Seeker.why: Arcane Strike is a Sneak Attack that always qualifies and lands as Force, the least-resisted type in the list, and Brilliant Edge at 13 adds Intelligence as Force to every weapon attack and makes that Force pierce Resistance. Auspicious Parry - take 1 damage instead of the hit - is the best survival reaction on any Rogue, and Lone Wolf's second reaction means you parry and still Uncanny Dodge. Spell Siphon and Disrupt are the enemy-caster answer a duo otherwise has no body to spare for.
uncertain: The whole kit runs on Sorcery Points: a pool of only 1 + Int modifier on a long rest, topped up only when enemies actually cast spells. Against a fight with no casters this body reverts to a plain Rogue, which is why `end` sits below the class floor.
Int on top of Dex is genuine MAD, and the free-off-hand plus light-armour requirement rules out dual-wielding and shields.

sorcerer/Draconic Bloodline (vanilla) +.why: Elemental Affinity now reaches Force (Amethyst, Cobalt, Eyrie Force), so Charisma modifier rides every dart and every damage instance of a type almost nothing resists — a per-hit rider on a scaling engine, and the only bloodline that also fixes the d6 die and the naked AC.
uncertain: st 4 and the Absolute Wrath cap both assume a Force ancestry; a Fire or Cold ancestry is locked to a commonly-resisted type and caps at 4 anyway, but loses a rung of realised damage.
rsc 0 ignores the Hallow ancestry's Sanctuary, which would be rung-2 prevention — taking it costs the damage identity the score is built on.

sorcerer/Wild Magic (vanilla) + Wild Mag.why: The 14228 spell list finally gives Wild Magic a control spine (Tasha's, Hypnotic Pattern, Confusion, Dominate Person) castable off sorcery points via Arcane Chaos, and Bend Luck is a two-reaction, non-concentration swing on any save in the fight — Mirror Image and Blink are what carry its durability.
uncertain: Every Arcane Chaos cast forces a surge, and a surge that Banishes or Confuses the caster removes half a two-body party; the scores treat the surge as neutral, which is optimistic for a duo.

sorcerer/Storm Sorcery (vanilla).why: Heart of the Storm bolts a free area rider onto every Lightning or Thunder cast, on top of the full Sorcerer pool's Call Lightning and Chain Lightning; the bonus-action fly is durability by never being reachable, and Lone Wolf's second bonus action removes its clash with Quickened.
uncertain: Locked to Lightning/Thunder, so under Absolute Wrath the damage axes cap at 4 from Act II without a resistance strip or a second type.

sorcerer/Shadow Magic (vanilla) + Shadow.why: Hound of Ill Omen is the rung-4 shape on a short-rest clock — a summoned third body that imposes disadvantage on one target's saves and costs no concentration, so it never competes with the partner's slot; Strength of the Grave is a repeating refusal to go down on a d6 chassis.
uncertain: Umbral Form is shipped twice (15855 and Expansion) at level 18 and the interaction is unverified; it lands outside Act II either way.
True Darkness is not installed, so no darkness-cheese durability.

sorcerer/Aberrant Mind.why: Psionic Sorcery casts Evard's Black Tentacles, Hunger of Hadar and Dominate Person for sorcery points equal to their level with no verbal or somatic components, turning the point pool into a second, cheaper casting clock; Psychic resistance and advantage on Charm and Fright saves patch the two effects most likely to remove a body.
uncertain: ctrl_a 4 rests on Evard's being repeatable off points rather than costing no concentration — it still holds concentration, so it is the Act II rung-5 named spell on a rung-3 clock. 3 is defensible.
Summon Beholderkin at L7 is a genuine extra body but only one, so act stops at 3.

sorcerer/Favored Soul.why: The only Charisma caster that gets Cleric healing at level 1 as Sorcerer spells, so Metamagic applies — Twinned Death Ward and Twinned Greater Restoration cover a two-body party outright, and Revivify plus Raise Dead answer the duo's worst failure mode; medium armour and shields at level 1 fix the class's naked-AC problem.
uncertain: rsc 4 not 5: it has prevention and restoration but no no-action outward source (no Twilight-Sanctuary-grade aura).
dur 3 on a d6 hit die is a judgement call — medium + shield + magic AC + self-healing is the mitigation actually applied, but the hit die is the joint-lowest in the game.
Scores assume a Life or Peace domain; Tempest or Light trades the rescue rung for aoe.

sorcerer/Wretched Soul.why: No published feature list, levels or progression; the class file marks the whole subclass unverified and listo-rules.md omits it from the surviving-subclass list. Listo added it for testing.

warlock/The Archfey.why: Fey Presence is area charm-or-fear off a short-rest charge with no concentration — the rung-4 clause — and Dominate Person at patron 9 lands on a short-rest pact slot rather than a long-rest one, so the control clock is the best in the patron set; nothing here is aimed at the partner and light armour with no shield is the floor.
uncertain: Archfey gets no 14th-level feature from Expansion and the class file records it as unverified whether another mod fills the gap; nothing was scored for it.

end 4 rather than the rubric's explicit 'Warlock 11 = 9 units' rung-2 anchor: Eldritch Blast is at-will with no clock, which is the rung-5 definition, and the 9 units fund everything else. The tension is real and applies to all five non-Psyker patrons here.

warlock/The Fiend.why: The only patron whose expanded list gives a real burst under Eldritch Cone — Fireball, Wall of Fire, Flame Strike — and the only one whose defensive kit is proportional: Fiendish Resilience is a resistance you re-pick every rest, on top of Dark One's Own Luck as a short-rest reroll.
uncertain: The burst half of aoe 4 is all Fire, a commonly resisted type; Eldritch Cone's Force is the unresisted half and it stops scaling at character 10, so this row is at its peak exactly at the judging point.
Hurl Through Hell is a 14 feature and is not counted.
end 4 versus the rubric's Warlock-11 rung-2 anchor — see the Archfey note; Eldritch Blast's at-will clock is what carries it.

warlock/The Great Old One.why: Evard's Black Tentacles at patron 7 comes off a short-rest pact slot, which is the rubric's top-of-ladder area control on a repeatable clock, and Mortal Reminder's area fear fires far more often than its text suggests because six Eldritch Blast beams a round make six crit checks; Entropic Ward spends the spare Reaction Lone Wolf hands over.
uncertain: ctrl_a 4 not 5 because Evard's still spends the one concentration slot; Mortal Reminder is the free layer under it but is crit-gated.
Create Thrall is a 14 feature and is not counted.
end 4 versus the rubric's Warlock-11 rung-2 anchor — see the Archfey note.

warlock/The Hexblade.why: The one patron that turns the chassis melee at level 1 — Hex Warrior puts Charisma on the weapon without waiting for Pact of the Blade — and Eldritch Smite off a short-rest pact slot is the rubric's named rung-4 repeatable burst channel under Thirsting Blade's Extra Attack and Hexblade's Curse's crit range; Accursed Spectre is a maintained third body.
uncertain: concentration false because Curse plus smites needs none, which is unusual for a caster and is the patron's quiet advantage in a pair holding only two slots.
Warlock grants no shield proficiency, so dur 2 rests on the Shield spell and Blur against a three-slot budget the rubric warns will not support casting Shield most rounds; 1 is defensible.
Master of Hexes is a 14 feature and is not counted. Mizora's Rewards modifies Hexblade's Pact alongside Pact of the Blade; the interaction was not in the read set.
end 4 versus the rubric's Warlock-11 rung-2 anchor — see the Archfey note.

warlock/The Celestial.why: The only Warlock with any outward rescue at all, and it is the good kind: Healing Light is a bonus-action heal spending no slot, so Lone Wolf's second bonus action buys two a turn alongside a full Action, and Revivify at patron 5 plus Greater Restoration at 9 both ride the short-rest pact clock rather than a long-rest one. Free Sacred Flame is also the save-based radiant answer to the high-AC targets Eldritch Blast's attack roll misses.
uncertain: rsc 4 rather than 3 rests on the clock rather than the ladder's literal rung-4 clause: there is no Death Ward or Sanctuary here, so no true prevention, but restoration on a short-rest clock plus bonus-action outward healing is what rung 4 exists to reward.
Healing Light's own pool is long-rest, so it is a per-day budget, not a per-fight one.
Searing Vengeance is a 14 feature and is not counted.
end 4 versus the rubric's Warlock-11 rung-2 anchor — see the Archfey note.

warlock/The Psyker.why: Warp turns every Eldritch Blast beam into a 3d10 Force detonation in a 3m radius, which is a genuinely repeatable at-will area engine in the least-resisted damage type — and Perils of the Warp pays for it in max hit points every turn, which is the one resource a duo cannot spare and the reason Endurance is the lowest in this whole assignment.
uncertain: end 2, not 4, is the load-bearing judgement here: the damage is at-will but the engine drains max HP (1d8 per turn of remaining duration at level 11+), and the rubric says hit points force more long rests than slots do. Gellar's Field is once per short rest and only blocks Perils for 2 turns.

It is explicitly unverified whether Warp detonations count as Eldritch Blast for Agonizing Blast or Mizora's IsEldritchBlastAlike rider system. If they do not, aoe 4 holds but st 3 and ctrl_s 3 are both a rung high.
Chaos Rift is a 14 feature and is not counted.
Listo added the DTO pack 'for testing'; the class file says to treat this patron as less settled than the rest.

wizard/Abjuration.why: Arcane Ward (cap 2x wizard level, ~26 at char 13) refilling for wizard level on every short rest is the only thing that makes a d6 robe survivable; Projected Ward spends the spare Lone Wolf reaction to eat the partner's damage on a short-rest clock, which is repeatable outward prevention rather than redirection. Offence is the generic wizard list.
uncertain: Spell Resistance lands at wizard 14, the top edge of the Act II band; scored at 12-13 without it, so the Act II value understates the back half of the act.

wizard/Bladesinging.why: The only Wizard with a real defensive floor: light armour plus +4 AC and +4 Con saves from Bladesong at 9, Song of Defence converting a slot into flat 5-per-level reduction, and Extra Attack at 6 for turns that should not cost a slot. Rescue is nil and the whole package is a long-rest resource (4 uses), which is exactly the clock Listo taxes.
uncertain: Bladesong, Extra Attack and cantrips are all concentration-free, so `concentration` is false on the subclass plan; a Bladesinger who wants Blur or Shadow Blade re-acquires the cost.
Song of Victory (+Int to weapon damage, the piece that would move `st` to 3) lands at 14, above the judging point.

wizard/Conjuration.why: Focused Conjuration at 10 makes damage unable to break concentration on a Conjuration spell, and the L6 off-list pick reaches the druid/cleric summon pool, so this is the Wizard that fields a summon set that cannot be knocked over. The bonus-action item conjurer is a small repeatable AoE and a trickle of outward potions; Ultimate Transposition extracts the partner. No defensive layer of its own.
uncertain: Whether Conjure Animals picked off-list inherits `13458`'s non-concentration-until-long-rest change is not confirmed; if it does not, `act` is 3 rather than 4.
The mod places its features at 3 and 6 against vanilla's 2 and 6 and the class file records the level-2 slot as unverified.

wizard/Divination.why: Portent replaces an attack roll or saving throw outright, and Expert Divination refunds dice on short rests, so it is a short-rest pool of guaranteed outcomes spent through the spare Lone Wolf reaction. That converts a slot control spell into no-fail single-target lockdown, blanks an incoming attack, and can be aimed at the partner's save, which is prevention rather than healing.
uncertain: Greater Portent at 14 is listed in Expansion's changelog but the class file flags it as unverified; not scored.

wizard/Enchantment.why: Hypnotic Gaze is charm-plus-incapacitate on one creature costing no slot and no concentration, and in this list it also strips the target's concentration; Split Enchantment doubles Hold Person and Dominate at the level encounters start fielding pairs. Instinctive Charm gives the spare reaction a job. Nothing outward, nothing durable.
uncertain: Listo enemies are markedly more save-capable than vanilla and bosses carry magic resistance, so a pure save-DC lockdown school is worth less here than the feature text reads.

wizard/Evocation.why: Empowered Evocation puts Intelligence on every evocation damage roll, which is a rider on every cast rather than a flat bonus, and Sculpt Spells matters more in a duo than a four-party because the partner is always inside the fireball. Slot count supports several 4th-5th tier AoE casts a fight. Zero rescue, zero durability, and the AoE is fire-and-cold heavy against Absolute Wrath's layered resistances.
uncertain: Overchannel's maximised burst arrives at 14, above the judging point.

wizard/Illusion.why: The thinnest base school. Illusory Self is a genuine once-per-rest 'this attack misses' on a d6 body and See Invisibility is short-rest, but a bonus-action Minor Illusion has little pull against Listo's reworked enemies and there is no scaling feature at all. Everything above the floor here comes from the wizard list, not the school.

wizard/Necromancy.why: Animate Dead++ removes the undead cap entirely, upcasts two more bodies per slot, moves the free Animate Dead to 5 and extends Undead Thralls' HP and proficiency-bonus damage to every undead owned; none of it costs concentration, so it stacks on top of Haste handed to the partner. That is the largest action-economy answer in the list. Inured to Undeath also blanks the max-HP-reduction effects Act II leans on. Grim Harvest is self-healing, so it sits in Durability.
uncertain: The undead are long-rest-bound bodies; `Necromancy Heals Undead` tops them up mid-fight but the pool itself does not refresh on a short rest.
Command Undead at 14 is in Expansion's changelog only and the class file flags it unverified.

wizard/Transmutation.why: The Transmuter's Stone is one of very few cross-character buffs a Wizard can simply leave on the other player - Constitution save proficiency or a damage resistance, permanent, no action, which is prevention rather than healing. Everything else is thin: Experimental Alchemy does not stack with other sources and Shapechanger is a blue jay. The stone cannot be on both bodies at once.

wizard/War Magic.why: A reaction-based AC and save spike plus an initiative bonus on a robe chassis, which uses the spare Lone Wolf reaction the way Bladesinging uses armour. Scored as the generic wizard list plus one mitigation reaction, because that is all the class file can confirm.
uncertain: The per-level feature table is images-only on the mod page: the actual numbers for Arcane Deflection, Tactical Wit, Power Surge and Durable Magic are unverified. Power Surge in particular could move `st` to 3 and Durable Magic could move `dur` to 3.

wizard/Order of Scribes.why: Formulaic Attunement ignores resistance to the attuned damage type and adds damage on top, which is the rubric's named exemption from the one-damage-type cap under Absolute Wrath and matters more here than its size suggests. The Spectral Mind is both a body and a remote casting position, which is real cover for a chassis with no third party member to block for it.
uncertain: Levels for Wizardly Quill and Awakened Spellbook and the exact Formulaic Attunement damage bonus are unverified (mod-page tables are images).
Attunement cannot be changed during combat, so the resistance-strip only covers the type you guessed before the fight.

wizard/Hexcraft.why: Four invocations by wizard 10 on an Intelligence chassis, and the Warlock-copying clause means Eldritch Blast with Agonising Blast is available - at-will single-target damage with a per-beam rider, which no other Wizard has. Ritual completion pays temp HP equal to ritual level plus wizard level, and level 10 is flat immunity to the charm and fear line, which is worth a great deal when losing either body ends the run. The slot-economy school in a 120-supply-per-long-rest game.
uncertain: Eldritch Blast is 1d8 per beam here, not 1d10, so the at-will engine is smaller than any outside math suggests.
Heart of Darkness's slot regeneration lands at 14, above the judging point.
Invocations cannot be changed once picked.

wizard/Hierophant.why: The rescue ceiling of the class and the only cross-list subclass actually wired in 10.2. By character 12-13 it holds all three rescue forms at once: prevention (Erudite Remedy grants the partner a chosen damage resistance as a bonus action at 18 m, pre-appliable before a known hit), restoration (Lesser and Greater Restoration always prepared, Raise Dead as a ritual at 10), and repeatable outward healing (Mass Healing Word plus a wizard-level pool of d6). Spirit Guardians is real repeatable area denial and Guardian of Faith is a zone that costs no concentration.
uncertain: Erudite Remedy refreshes on a long rest only; Turn the Otherworldly and Warding Rejuvenation are the short-rest pieces and Warding Rejuvenation lands at 14.

wizard/School of Death.why: The highest sustained single-target damage of the schools and the only one that converts Arcane Recovery charges into damage: Touch of Death is 5 + twice wizard level necrotic for two charges, roughly three times per long rest, on top of Negative Energy Infusion's per-turn 1d8 and doubled necrotic cantrips from Reaper. Inescapable Destruction strips necrotic resistance, which is the clause that keeps a mono-type body off the Absolute Wrath cap. It gives no defensive layer at all.

wizard/School of Bombardment.why: Scored as the bare Wizard chassis - full list access, robe durability, no subclass uplift - because that is the only part of this school that can be defended from source. The published identity is long-range ordnance, so the real profile is probably an AoE and single-target lift over this floor.
uncertain: SEVERE: every mechanic of this subclass is unverified. The per-level feature list is published only as images and the mod.io mirror is JavaScript-gated, so no feature, level or number was read. The scores here are a chassis floor, not a reading of the subclass; anyone comparing rows should treat this one as unscored until it is read off the level-up screen.
